query: Over 2015-2024, exactly one economy in the 27 advanced economies with an IMF World Economic Outlook output-gap estimate (Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Cyprus, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Korea, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, the United Kingdom, the United States) had real output growth above 6.0% a year. On average per year, how many percentage points of that economy's growth came from improvements in efficiency, once the contributions of the capital stock and of employment are set aside? Convention: Cobb-Douglas production with a capital share of 0.33; build the capital stock from the WEO investment ratio and real GDP with 10% annual depreciation, starting from first-available-year investment divided by (0.10 + average real GDP growth over that year and the next nine); employment from the WEO.

text.text: Identifies growth accounting with a Cobb-Douglas production function (capital stock from investment by perpetual inventory, employment, TFP as residual).
text.accept: full = Cobb-Douglas growth accounting with TFP residual; capital share 0.33 and depreciation 10% (Mexico 2004 Art. IV convention) or close alternative acceptable (capital share 0.3-0.4)

data.text: Uses WEO series: NGDP_R, NID_NGDP, LE.

computation.accept: full = within tolerance; capital stock by perpetual inventory (delta 10%, K_1980=I_1980/(delta+g)), capital share 0.33, TFP = gY - a*gK - (1-a)*gL; correct country identification required (hidden)

assembled_from: Mexico 2004 Art IV growth-accounting box (270b189d, block 125) and WEO Apr 2015 Ch.3 (3ed94aa0, blocks 1055-1059)
provenance.selection: seeded draw (20261030), distinct country within style where possible

gold_report_note: No corpus report states these values; gold is recomputed from the frozen WEO vintage by formula (formula-validated, no published figure).
distractors: labour-productivity or per-capita income decomposition (employment rate)
predicate: among the 27 economies with WEO employment data, average real GDP growth (NGDP_R) > 6.0% per year over 2015-2024
